elements.element: The Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of New York.
elements.evidence: Section 28.1 expressly states that the Agreement is governed exclusively by the laws of the State of New York.

elements.element: State courts located in New York County, New York are included in the designated forum.
elements.evidence: Section 28.2 designates the state courts located in New York County, New York.

elements.element: Federal courts located in New York County, New York are included in the designated forum.
elements.evidence: Section 28.2 designates the federal courts located in New York County, New York.

elements.element: Jurisdiction is exclusive to the designated New York County state and federal courts.
elements.evidence: Section 28.2 gives those courts exclusive jurisdiction, and the injunctive-relief provision is confined to “those courts,” so it does not create an outside-forum exception.

elements.element: The chosen governing law is Delaware law, California law, or the laws of England and Wales.
elements.evidence: Section 28.1 instead selects the laws of the State of New York.

elements.element: If Delaware law is selected, courts in Delaware are selected as the dispute forum.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because the rendered clause selects New York law, not Delaware law.

elements.element: If California law is selected, courts in California are selected as the dispute forum.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because the rendered clause selects New York law, not California law.

elements.element: If the laws of England and Wales are selected, the courts of London are selected as the dispute forum.
elements.evidence: The condition is demonstrably absent because the rendered clause selects New York law, not the laws of England and Wales.

result.reason: The operative language fully implements the preferred New York governing-law and exclusive New York County forum position. Confining temporary injunctive relief to the same designated courts is necessary to avoid undermining exclusivity. The edits do not disturb unrelated personal-jurisdiction or objection-waiver terms. The fallback is not independently satisfied because none of its permitted governing laws is selected.
